newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Moody's assigns Aaa to ARMS II Fund II bond.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Moody's assigns Aaa to ARMS II Fund II bond.

text.p: Moody's Investors Service has assigned a rating Aaa to the A$485 million senior tranch 1 bonds to be issued by Permanent Custodians Ltd in its capacity as trustee of the ARMS II Fund II.
Australia Residential Mortgage Securities (ARM) programme is established by Australian Mortgage Securities Ltd, which is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Barclays Bank Plc.
It also assigned an A1 to the A$15 million of subordinated Tranche 2 bonds in the issue.

Moody's said the ratings are based on the quality of the collateral in the form of residential mortgage loans and the mortgage policies provided by Housing Loans Insurance Corporation (rated Aaa) and MGICA Ltd (rated A1).
The policies cover default losses in an amount equal to 100 percent of the principal amount of each loan.
The rating also reflects the liquidity support provided by a cash reserve account, timely interest coverage from the insurance polices and deferral of manager's fees.

The rating is also based on the strength of the legal documents setting out the obligations of the various parties in the programme, and on the 3.0 percent subordination of the tranche 1 bonds by tranche 2.
AMS is responsible for the origination, management and servicing of mortgages securitised through the ARMS II programme.
AMS, which was orignally establised by the Australian Mutual Provident Society in 1987, has arranged the issuance of over A$2.0 billion in mortgage backed securities.
